subject: Medivance: starter subsidy & multi-product bundle exception request
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greene <t.greene@medivance.com>; Sarah Patel <sarah@medivance.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Medivance: starter subsidy & multi-product bundle exception request

Tom / Sarah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the ask so internal folks have context.

Medivance is looking to sign a 12-month contract covering three Redwood products: Inference (hosted API), Dedicated capacity for an initial pilot (~4 GPUs), and Private (VPC) for production. Their procurement sendover asked for: a 40% "starter subsidy" on list rates for months 1-3, waiver of onboarding fees (~$15k), and a one-month free seat allocation for their first 50 active users. They cited budget timing and a potential multi-product expansion to the rest of their org in Q4 as the rationale.

They've pushed a target start date of July 1 to align with a grant disbursement. They are also requesting a 60-day SOC2 evidence turnaround (we can meet with our compliance team but it increases delivery risk).

Ask to the group: this is outside our standard commercial guardrails (starter subsidy > 25% and onboarding waiver require VP/CFO signoff). Can Marissa / Kimberly / Lauren review for exception and signoff guidance? I attached a revised commercial_summary and the latest pricing matrix with modeled net ARR and margin impact.

Attachments: [attachment: commercial_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32 KB)], [attachment: medivance_mop_v3.pdf (proposal, 180 KB)], [attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 54 KB)]

Key quick points:
- Projected committed ARR at year 1 (post-subsidy): $420k
- If we grant 40% starter subsidy (months 1-3) blended revenue reduces by ~$36k in year 1; first-year gross margin drops ~6 percentage points under base assumptions.
- Tradeoff: High strategic value (healthcare reference, likely cross-sell), procurement requests are time-sensitive.

I recommend: either (A) grant a capped starter subsidy (25%) tied to clear KPIs + onboarding fee credited back on milestone; or (B) grant full subsidy but only for a 6-month limited pilot with automatic rollback and no onboarding waiver.

Happy to take this to the VP/CFO thread if you want a short memo template.

—Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-06-16T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Medivance: starter subsidy & multi-product bundle exception request

Mateo — thanks for the clear summary and the files. Looping internally so we have a single thread for approval.

I can't approve a 40% open-ended subsidy without a concrete mitigation plan. Before I escalate to finance/CFO, can you please provide the following by EOD tomorrow:
1) Simple P&L: list price vs. proposed effective revenue over 12 months (I need the blended ARR numbers broken out by product).
2) Adoption milestones tied to subsidy release (e.g., X seats deployed / Y API QPS / proof of integration to Private).
3) A contingency clause: if public reference or expansion doesn't materialize by month 9, we revert to standard pricing and recoup a portion of the subsidy.
4) Procurement's official PO timeline and any procurement constraints that make July 1 a hard deadline.

Counterproposal I'm comfortable presenting to finance: 25% starter subsidy for months 1-2 only, onboarding fee credited after successful integration milestone, and a one-time professional service discount (not full waiver). This preserves economics while giving Medivance runway.

Marissa
Senior Commercial Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks. P&L and milestones attached, plus a short risk memo. Highlights below pulled from the attachments (commercial_summary.xlsx + redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx).

Summary numbers (all $):
- List ARR (12 months, no discounts): $520,000
- Proposed effective ARR (with 40% starter subsidy months 1-3): $484,000
- Delta to list (year 1): -$36,000 (one-time impact concentrated in Q3)
- Estimated gross margin change (year 1): -6.2 percentage points (assuming current cost per token and reserved capacity needs)

Adoption milestones tied to subsidy release (proposed):
- Subsidy tranche 1 (months 0–1): released upon signed SOW and PO; onboarding fee credited only after dedicated pool provisioned and first production workload observed.
- Subsidy tranche 2 (months 2–3): released on successful integration (alpha tests: API calls >1k/day for 7 consecutive days and Private VPC network connectivity validated).
- Clawback: if expansion to additional business units does not begin by month 9, we recoup up to 50% of subsidy via credit against renewal or next invoice.

Strategic justification: Medivance is a potential enterprise reference in the cardiac imaging vertical; they have active integration teams and two additional product teams (analytics + clinical automation) that signaled interest contingent on pilot success. We modeled a 35% chance of cross-sell in 12 months yielding incremental $300–450k ARR.

Procurement timeline: Tom confirmed internal PO must be issued before July 5 to hit their grant draw. They also want SOC2 evidence within 60 days; our compliance team has flagged extra effort but said it's doable if we prioritize.

I've attached the (redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx) showing net present value at different subsidy levels and a short memo (medivance_mop_v3.pdf) with recommended contract language for staged subsidy and clawback.

Suggested escalation ask for VP/CFO memo: "Approve starter subsidy up to 35% (months 1–3) conditional on staged milestones, onboarding fee credited after provisioning, and 50% clawback if expansion milestone not met by month 9. Finance to sign final paperwork."

If you want, I can convert this into an executive one-pager for Kimberly to sign.

—Mateo

Date: 2026-06-18T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Approved: Medivance starter subsidy (conditional)

Team / Tom — after reviewing the numbers and the staged milestones, I approve an exception with the following binding conditions: 

1) Subsidy cap: up to 35% starter subsidy for months 1–3 only (not 40%).
2) Milestones: tranche releases as outlined in Mateo's memo (provisioning, integration, API activity). No release without evidence.
3) Onboarding fee: not waived up front. Onboarding fee ($15k) will be credited in full after provisioning and first production traffic observed.
4) Clawback: if expansion milestone is not met by month 9 (defined as signed order for any additional product line or 3x active-seat increase), Finance will apply a 50% credit recoup against renewal or outstanding invoices.
5) SOC2: compliance will provide an accelerated evidence packet; any additional compliance work outside standard scope will be billed to the customer.

Mateo — please convert these conditions into redlines for the SOW and route to Legal/Finance. Finance should prepare the credit terms and include the clawback language verbatim. Once the SOW contains these conditions, I will sign.

Kimberly Park
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
